challenge.label: The Challenge
challenge.heading: The Non Hazardous Waste Industry At A Glance

points.text: With the US producing over 254 million tons of solid waste annually and about 140 million tons going to landfills, the need for alternative waste management solutions is urgent.
Alternative Engineered Fuel volumes to rise from 297,000 to 502,000 tons (6.07%) by 2032.
Rapidly emerging as a sustainable solution to diverting waste from landfills.

technology.heading: Why Cement Plants Need Alternative Fuels
technology.description: 200 lbs of engineered fuel per ton of cement made added instead of coal.

diagram.alt: Cement manufacturing from quarry, crusher, transport and raw mill through kiln and preheater/precalcinator, cooler, cement mill and logistics. Engineered fuel is injected at the preheater/precalcinator. CO2 emissions: 3%, 51% chemical calcination process, 34% fuels for heat, and 12%.

about.label: About
about.heading: Waste4Energy, LLC.
about.intro: Backed by 4 executives with expertise in waste management, recycling, and land development, W4E is positioned to provide innovative recycling to the projected demand exceeding 100,000 tons in 2 undisclosed territory by 2026, leveraging the team's, comprehensive knowledge, and industry connections for substantial growth.

team.name: Paul Bordelon
bio: Over 15 years of experience in corporate sales, environmental services, and project management.
Proven track record in achieving business growth, operational excellence, and establishing national contracts with Fortune 500 companies.

team.name: Jeff Gloyd
bio: Over 25 years of experience managing and building waste processing companies in both private and Fortune 500 sectors.
Proven track record of establishing the largest e-scrap processor in North America and managing international sales teams.

team.name: Torry Ingram
bio: Two decades of experience in the hazardous and non-hazardous waste industry.
Past ten years focused on supplying and managing tens of thousands of tons of waste fuels for cement kilns.

team.name: Grant Williams
bio: Since 2018, has worked for JW Development on site analysis and selection for projects in Texas, Florida, and North Carolina.
Evaluates all aspects of land feasibility for private joint ventures and multi-billion-dollar REITs.

vision.label: Our Roadmap
vision.heading: Our Vision
vision.text: By building three strategic sites in Texas, Alabama, and the Western US by 2026, we will revolutionize waste management, enhance energy recovery using innovative recycling that transforms non-hazardous waste into alternative, eco-friendly fuels for cement kilns, championing sustainability, excellence, and efficiency.
